lines.say: A pathogen is an agent that causes disease in a host.
Infection is the guest arriving. Disease is the guest wrecking the house.
So you can be infected with no disease, like an asymptomatic carrier.
Opportunistic pathogens only cause disease when the host's defences fall.
Prions are misfolded proteins. They make normal copies misfold too.
Viruses are nucleic acid in a protein coat. They need a host cell to copy themselves.
Bacteria, fungi, protists and parasitic animals are all cellular.

draw.alt: Pathogens arranged from non-cellular to multicellular

lines.say: Antibiotics hit peptidoglycan walls or 70 S ribosomes. Viruses have neither.
In Tasmanian devils, the cancer cells themselves spread by biting.
Virulence is how much harm a pathogen does to its host.
Adhesins attach. Invasion enzymes spread. Capsules dodge immune cells.
Exo means exits. Exotoxins are proteins the bacterium secretes, like tetanus toxin.
Endo means embedded. Endotoxin is lipopolysaccharide in the Gram negative outer membrane.
Antigenic variation changes surface molecules, so immune memory misses them.
Routes include contact, droplets, faecal oral, vectors and vertical transmission.
Zoonoses jump from animals. Hendra virus goes from flying foxes to horses to people.
R nought above 1 spreads. Below 1, it fades.

draw.alt: One case infects two, each infects two more

lines.say: Herd immunity needs about 1 minus 1 over R nought immune.
Measles at R nought 15: 1 minus one fifteenth is about 93 percent.
Barriers come first: skin, mucus, cilia, stomach acid, lysozyme in tears.
Innate immunity is fast and non specific. Every animal and plant has it.
Plants kill their own infected cells. That's the hypersensitive response.
Adaptive immunity is slower, specific, and has memory. Vertebrates have it.
In 1950, myxoma virus was released, and it killed most infected rabbits.
Strains that killed too fast gave mosquitoes less time to pick them up.
So intermediate virulence became most common. That's the virulence transmission trade-off.
Rabbits evolved too. Exposed populations died at 30 percent, not 90.
Pathogens don't always become harmless. Selection maximises transmission.
Infection and disease are not the same thing.
Antibiotics don't treat viruses.
Nothing evolves in order to adapt. Selection acts on existing variation.
Exotoxins exit. Endotoxins are embedded.
